title: Two-Phase Commit (2PC)
description: Learn the two-phase commit protocol and its limitations in microservices.

data.text: Two-phase commit (2PC) is a distributed transaction protocol that attempts to provide ACID guarantees across multiple services. While 2PC works in theory, it is rarely recommended for microservices due to blocking behavior and reduced availability.

2PC has two phases: prepare and commit. In the prepare phase, the coordinator asks all participants if they are ready to commit. If all agree, the coordinator sends a commit command in the second phase. If any participant disagrees, all are rolled back.

data.title: 2PC Limitations
items: Blocking: Participants hold locks during prepare phase
Single point of failure: Coordinator failure blocks the transaction
Reduced availability: Network partition means no commit or rollback
Performance: Two round-trips add significant latency
No automatic recovery: Manual intervention may be needed

data.title: The Blocking Problem
data.text: In 2PC, if the coordinator crashes after sending prepare but before sending commit, participants are blocked indefinitely. They cannot commit or roll back without coordinator input.

data.title: Example: 2PC Transaction Flow
data.code: A two-phase commit across Inventory and Payment services.

# Phase 1: Prepare
Coordinator -> Inventory: Prepare to deduct stock?
Coordinator -> Payment: Prepare to charge?

Inventory: Yes, ready to commit
Payment: Yes, ready to commit

# Phase 2: Commit
Coordinator -> Inventory: Commit
Coordinator -> Payment: Commit

# Problem: What if Payment says No?
# All must roll back
# What if Coordinator crashes after prepare?
# All services are blocked!

data.caption: Two-phase commit protocol
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Coordinator
    participant I as Inventory
    participant P as Payment
    C->>I: Prepare
    C->>P: Prepare
    I-->>C: Ready
    P-->>C: Ready
    C->>I: Commit
    C->>P: Commit

items.question: When should I use 2PC?
items.answer: Rarely. Only when you absolutely need strong consistency and cannot use eventual consistency. Even then, consider three-phase commit or other protocols.

items.question: What is three-phase commit (3PC)?
items.answer: 3PC adds a pre-commit phase to reduce blocking. It addresses some 2PC issues but is still complex and rarely used in practice.

items.question: Are there any databases that support distributed transactions?
items.answer: Some databases like Spanner and CockroachDB provide distributed ACID transactions. However, they are limited to their own ecosystem and do not help with cross-service transactions.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: 2PC provides ACID across services but at high cost
Saga pattern is almost always a better choice
data.takeaway: Avoid 2PC in microservices; use Saga pattern for distributed transactions instead.
